“In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, if you require a
disability related modification or accommodation to attend or participate in this
meeting, including auxiliary aids or services, please call the City Clerk’s office at
310-952-1720 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.” (Government Code Section
54954.2)
PUBLIC INFORMATION

The public may address the members of the City Council on any matters within the
jurisdiction of the City Council or on any items on the agenda of the City Council
during the designated public comment periods. There will be two Oral
Communication sessions: one for Agendized Items (comment about items ON the
agenda) and the other for non-Agendized items (comment about items NOT on the
Agenda). The Oral Communications portion of the agenda is limited to a duration of
one hour unless otherwise approved by the City Council. Comment time is normally
3 minutes depending on the number of speakers.

Because of the threat of COVID-19 (the “Coronavirus”) you are urged to take all
appropriate health safety precautions. Wearing masks is not required but is highly
recommended while inside Carson City Hall. Temperatures will be checked for those
experiencing any symptoms of COVID-19, prior to entering the City Hall.

PUBLIC VIEWING AVAILABLE BY:

- Livestream on the City’s website: The meeting will be streamed live over the
internet  via:  www.carsonca.gov  or on  Youtube:
www.youtube.com/c/CityofCarsonCaliforniaOfficialYouTubePage

- Cable TV: Spectrum (Channel 35) and ATT (Channel 99)

CITY OF CARSON  Page 1
 Housing Authority/Successor Agency/City Council  AGENDA  TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 19, 2023

IF YOU ARE NOT ABLE TO ATTEND THE MEETING IN-PERSON, PUBLIC COMMENTS
CAN BE SUBMITTED BEFORE THE MEETING AT/VIA:

- Email: Public comments can be emailed to cityclerk@carsonca.gov. The cut-off
time to submit any email communications is 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting.

- Written: Written comments can be dropped off at the City Clerk’s Office or in the
white box outside City Hall. The cut-off time to submit any written communications is
3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Written comments dropped off at the City
Clerk’s Office or at the white box or any email received will not be read aloud at
Council Meeting but will be circulated to the City Council and incorporated into the
record.

PUBLIC INFORMATION

The public may address the members of the City Council on any matters within the jurisdiction of the City Council or on any items on the agenda of the City Council during the designated public comment periods. There will be two Oral Communication sessions: one for Agendized Items (comment about items ON the agenda) and the other for non-Agendized items (comment about items NOT on the Agenda). The Oral Communications portion of the agenda is limited to a duration of one hour unless otherwise approved by the City Council. Comment time is normally 3 minutes depending on the number of speakers.

Because of the threat of COVID-19 (the “Coronavirus”) you are urged to take all appropriate health safety precautions. Wearing masks is not required but is highly recommended while inside Carson City Hall. 3.. REPORT FROM CAPTAIN JONES OF CARSON SHERIFF'S STATION Proclamation presented and photos taken 

After presentation, Mayor Davis- Holmes stated that there is a presentation by Reata from ISPM on charging station updates. Two slides were presented and a preview of the charging stations to come. The mayor wants regular updates on charging stations at each meeting so everyone is on the same page until the projects are complete. 

Councilman Hicks thanked Reta for bringing this information to council. And mentioned that the city is on the verge of generating its own energy. 
Councilman Dear thanked her for the presentation and asked if Tesla has changed their policy about allowing other cars to use the stations. Reta shared that they are testing other cars but other cars have trouble reaching the charging cables. A newer model, version 4, is available that has a longer charging cable and we are waiting to hear back if we are getting version 3 or version 4. Version 3 does come with an extra adapter to allow for other cars to charge. 
Councilman Dear also asked about managing parking in light of charging stations at parks. Reta shared that it is up to the city to determine how citations will work with charging station and parking spaces. 
Councilman Dear asked if there will be a cost to the public for charging stations. The charging stations will not be free.

35.. CONSIDER ADOPTION OF THE CITY'S ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT STRATEGIC PLAN (CITY COUNCIL) City Manager introduces Director of Finance William Jefferson and Senior Budget Analyst Ralston Turner to present information requested by Mayor Davis-Holmes 

Quarterly Report on ARPA and projects that are financed by these funds. 
march 11, 2021, President Biden and Congress approved a 1.9 trillion dollars stimulus package to help municipalities with COVID impacted expenses. Carson received 17.8 million dollars. 
There's still 5.5 million dollars year to date left to spend. 

City-wide slurry seal was awarded 3.3 million dollars. Remaining 25%. Mayor asked about if that's all the streets or not. Director Arlington Rogers answered and said it is the most impacted streets that adds service life. 
Mayor asks for a report every month on updates of all public works projects as it relates to street maintenance. Councilman Dear asked that all council signatures be on the letters that go out to residents about street maintenance. 
Ralston continued with his presentation on other funds allocation in various departments. 
Director William Jefferson spoke about the small business grant program. 
127 applicants and 46 have been approved in the amount of $875,000. 
Mayor wanted council to consider increasing the fund so that all businesses that are hurting as a result of inflation, high gas prices, etc. 
Mayor makes a motion to increase the fund and MPT second the motion. 
Under discussion, Councilman Dear asked about how much we increase it by $900,000. 
There are 75 businesses that have applied, the estimation is that about 52 businesses will be approved.
Right bow there is a balance of $400,000. That plus $900,000 will make 1.3 million dollars to make the account whole. 
The $900,000 would be ARPA money and general fund. 
The vote was unanimous.
The mayor asked to return if they need more money.
The budget resolution has to come back at the next council meeting.
